title: Whether the ZTC Terraform provider protects predefined traffic rules

checks.do: Which rules in the plan are predefined or default rules, before any destroy or resource-block removal in a configuration that manages Cloud Connector traffic rules: list the rule IDs in the plan.
Whether each rule's `defaultRule` or `predefined` flag is set, checked through the console or API, since the three resources never read that flag.
Whether the validators' fixed names match the predefined rules on the tenant, since they test the name only.
Whether a destroy of a predefined rule would be refused, since the provider sends the delete without a check and the API's answer is open.

guards-match-fixed-names.statement: The forwarding-rule and DNS-rule resources each define a validator that rejects deletion of a rule only when its name is one of a short hard-coded list (for forwarding rules, six names such as "ZPA Forwarding Rule" and "Client Connector to ZPA"; for DNS rules, two). The validators test the name only, not any default or predefined flag on the rule.

quotes: req.Name == "ZPA Forwarding Rule" || req.Name == "Direct rule for Zscaler Cloud Endpoints"
req.Name == "Client Connector to ZPA" || req.Name == "ZPA Pool For Stray Traffic"
req.Name == "ZPA Resolver" || req.Name == "Redirect Resolution of Zscaler Domains to WAN CTR"

log-guard-uses-dns-names.statement: The log-forwarding validator tests for the same two names as the DNS-rule validator ("ZPA Resolver" and "Redirect Resolution of Zscaler Domains to WAN CTR"), not for any name written for log rules.

quotes: req.Name == "ZPA Resolver" || req.Name == "Redirect Resolution of Zscaler Domains to WAN CTR"

forwarding-delete-skips-guard.statement: The forwarding-rule Delete reads the rule ID and sends the API delete. It does not fetch the rule and does not call validatePredefinedRules.
forwarding-delete-skips-guard.conditions: Rests on the absence of a call. The same search at other tags was not run.

resources-ignore-default-flag.statement: The three traffic-rule resources never read the rule's default or predefined flag. Only the log-rule data source copies default_rule into state.
resources-ignore-default-flag.conditions: Rests on an absence. Searched ztc/ at v0.2.0 and HEAD, case-insensitively, for DefaultRule, default_rule, Predefined and predefined, including schema keys and expand/flatten functions: the only reads are in the log-rule data source; other hits are comments and the name validators. The SDK rule models do carry these fields; the provider resources never read them.

destroy-sends-delete-for-protected-rules.statement: A terraform destroy, or removing the resource block, of a predefined traffic rule that is under management (for example after an import) sends the API delete for it with no provider-side refusal, for forwarding, DNS and log rules alike.
destroy-sends-delete-for-protected-rules.conditions: Depends on the rule being in state (a predefined rule enters a resource's state by import, since Terraform did not create it), and on the API then accepting the delete. Whether the API refuses to delete predefined rules is not known from the provider code (gap api-predefined-delete). If the API refuses, the apply fails with the API's error instead of the provider's, and the protection is the server's alone.

api-predefined-delete.title: Whether the ZTC API refuses to delete predefined traffic rules
api-predefined-delete.blocks: saying whether an unguarded delete removes a predefined rule or only returns an error
api-predefined-delete.detail: The provider code only shows that it sends the delete. In a scratch tenant, import a predefined forwarding, DNS and log rule, run destroy, and record the API response and whether the rule still exists.

predefined-log-rule-names.title: Names of the predefined log-forwarding rules
predefined-log-rule-names.blocks: saying whether the log-rule validator would protect any real log rule if it were called
predefined-log-rule-names.detail: The validator lists DNS-rule names. List the log rules in a scratch tenant and compare their predefined names with the validator's two entries.
